verdicts.why: A floor of a building is named without any attitude toward it.
In the 'at present' sense it only places something in time; the emphatic 'really, surprisingly' flavour in the sentences belongs to a different sense.
Putting something into operation is a plain act; the word takes no side on it.
A computer program is named as a category, with no approval or dismissal built in.
The work of applying something, including diligence in the sentences, is described rather than judged.
A medicinal preparation for the skin is a neutral technical name.
A pigment or dye is a plain material term with no attitude attached.
Naming vividness or variety in something describes a quality; any approval comes from valuing the quality, not from the word.
Timbre is a neutral descriptive term in music.
A quark property in physics is pure terminology with no attitude.
The teaching profession is named plainly, with no judgement of those in it.
A building for meetings or entertainment is a neutral label.
Calling a large house a hall names its kind and scale, not the speaker's attitude toward it.
The great room of a manor or castle is a plain architectural term.
A student residence building is named without judgement.
A university teaching building is a neutral institutional label.
The psychological sense of a habit is technical and takes no side on the behaviour.
The legal right to enjoy property is a term of art with no attitude.
Economic utilization of goods is neutral technical vocabulary.
In the 'lay claim to' sense ('I do not pretend to possess equal frankness') the word asserts a claim without implying falseness; the suggestion of sham belongs to the feigning sense.
Going in search of or hunting for something describes the action without judging the pursuer.
Putting forged money into circulation is a legal term naming an offence; the referent is bad but the word itself is a neutral term of art.
A course of reasoning is named plainly; whether the reasoning is good or bad is said by other words.
A plot summary of a literary work is a neutral literary term.
A value passed to a function is pure programming terminology.
